notes: Three own pages read, all HTTP 200 and not thin (home, pricing, home builders). Six cited pages read for causes (the per-vendor maximum); thedigitalprojectmanager.com answered 403 and is a cause candidate only, so it is not in needs_browser_read. Judgement calls: C08 and C10 are classed true and C09 wrong on the pricing page's '$199 per month' plus 'Save 20% on an annual subscription' (20% off $199 is $159.20); the snapshot does not print $159 itself. For the reviewer only: the raw pricing HTML carries data-annual-users="159,16,12,8,4" and data-monthly-users="199,20,15,10,5", which agree, but this was not used to class. C02 includes two Claude answers that attach the $20 user rate to an annual-billing sentence; the published $20 is the monthly-plan rate ($16 annual). C07 cause not found: no cited page read carries a $99 price. Derived configuration prices (C21, C22) are coded as pricing statements because they state a price; they follow from the published table. Evaluative 'transparent pricing' lines and review ratings were not coded. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser snapshot exists for JobTread and no claim was unverifiable for a blocked or thin page, so nothing was re-classed. The gap lines and tables added no claim: the table cells 'From ~$159/mo', '$159/mo', '$199/mo + $20/user', '~$199/mo' and '~$199+/mo' restate prices the same answers already carry in prose (C01, C02, C08, C09), the comparison tables with JobTread as a column header list features only, and the rest are features or about other vendors. Consistency check: C06 (custom quote against a published list price and per-user table), C07 (about $99 against $199 monthly or about $159 annual), C09 ($199 billed annually against the page's monthly-plan headline, whose $20 user rate the table puts in the Monthly Plan column, with 20% off annual) and C15 (free trial against 'We don't offer a free trial') stay wrong; each contradiction is on the vendor's own pricing page for the same single plan.
